name: prompt-bench
description: Prompt-Bench desktop app for Windows 11 (Electron + React + Vite)
//author: electron-builder warns "author is missed" without this and leaves the installer's Publisher field blank.
author: Rahul Ranjan
//main: Electron's entry point. Must be CommonJS, which is why there is no "type": "module" field.

scripts.//dev: Runs Vite and Electron together. -k kills both if either dies, so Ctrl+C leaves no orphan node.exe.
scripts.//dev:web: Browser-only mode at http://localhost:5173. No Electron, so no API key and no saving.
scripts.//dev:electron: Electron would show a blank window if it beat Vite to the port, so wait for the port first.
scripts.//start: Production smoke test: build, then load dist/ over file:// with the real CSP. --prod is required because running from source is never "packaged".
scripts.//dist: Produces a Windows .exe installer in release/. --publish never is load-bearing: electron-builder auto-publishes when it detects CI, which would fight the release workflow's own gh release create (and fail without GH_TOKEN). One publisher, chosen explicitly.
scripts.dist: npm run build && electron-builder --win --publish never && node scripts/zip-installer.mjs

//targets: build.win.target: nsis is the installer, zip is the portable build (unzip and run, nothing installed). scripts/zip-installer.mjs then wraps the installer, so every published asset is an archive rather than a bare .exe. Note: comments cannot live inside "build" - electron-builder schema-validates it and rejects unknown keys.
//dependencies: @anthropic-ai/sdk is used by the MAIN process, so it must be a runtime dep - a devDependency would be missing from the packaged .exe.
